name: Chicken 65 Totopos
line: Our fusion take on South Indian Chicken 65, crisp spiced chicken designed to be eaten with fresh masa totopos.
inspiration: South Indian “65” and Mexican totopos. Our own pairing of the two.

name: Chaat Elote
line: Charred corn with chile, lime and a crisp topping, intended to taste like street corn from two roadsides.
inspiration: Mexican elote and Indian bhutta and chaat. A fusion built on shared lime-salt-heat logic.

name: Dal-Frijol Dip
line: A slow-simmered black lentil and bean dip with a spiced-butter finish, for tearing bread and chips.
inspiration: Dal makhani technique and frijoles de olla. Our own dish.

name: Hefe-Brined Wings
line: Wings designed to be brined in a house wheat beer (which needs a brewery), tossed in one of three sauces.
inspiration: Our own dish; a link between kitchen and brewhouse (needs a brewery to exist).

name: Mango Habanero Gobi
line: Cauliflower that still tastes of cauliflower, in a mango and habanero glaze, to share. An appetizer, not a taco.
inspiration: Our own shareable, echoing Indian gobi preparations such as Gobi 65 and tandoori gobi. Fusion.

name: Paneer Tikka Taco
line: Charred yogurt-marinated paneer with green salsa and pineapple, intended to stay tender in a corn tortilla.
inspiration: Paneer tikka from the tandoor tradition, put in a taco. Fusion; our own composition.

name: Malabar-Pepper Fish Taco
line: Pepper-coconut marinated fish with cabbage and lime on a coastal taco.
inspiration: Kerala-coast flavours with a Baja or Yucatán-style fish taco. The “Malabar” name needs cultural review.

name: Tandoori Lamb Taco
line: Our own dish: charred, yogurt-marinated lamb in the tandoori manner, grilled and tucked into a flour tortilla.
inspiration: Inspired by Punjabi tandoori marination and Sonoran grilling and tortillas. Not a historical or traditional dish.

name: Goat Birria, Sealed-Pot Braise
line: Goat braised slowly in a chile adobo in a sealed pot, with a consommé to dip.
inspiration: Jalisco goat birria and a sealed, dum-style braise. Dipped, griddled tacos are a later Tijuana-style adaptation; ours uses goat. Our own composition.

name: Butter Chicken & Roasted Poblano Quesadilla
line: Butter-chicken sauce, roasted poblano and melting cheese in a griddled flour tortilla.
inspiration: Butter chicken from North India and the Mexican quesadilla con rajas. Fusion.

name: Toasted Seed & Chile Vegetable Bowl
line: Vegetables in a sauce of toasted nuts, seeds and dried chile, intended to be neither a mole nor a curry.
inspiration: Our own dish. The sauce logic echoes mole and salan, which is an analogy and not a shared history. Working name: Mole-Salan Bowl.

name: Cardamom Churros
line: Crisp churros dusted with cardamom sugar, with a dark jaggery-chocolate sauce.

name: Paneer Tikka Pizza
line: Tandoor-style paneer on a high-heat flatbread.
inspiration: Fusion, with pizza as a third tradition. Waiting on a kitchen and oven decision.

name: Dum Biryani
line: Layered rice and marinated chicken or vegetables, sealed and steamed. The name is held until a Hyderabadi cook confirms it.
inspiration: Biryani traditions. We will not call it Hyderabadi unless it earns that name.

name: Mushroom & Fenugreek Quesadilla
line: Mushrooms with epazote and fenugreek leaf in a griddled quesadilla.
inspiration: Fusion; the bitter-herb pairing is unproven.

name: Goat Birria Pizza (special only)
line: Goat birria on a flatbread with consommé on the side. Only if it beats the birria taco.
